command: uv run python spikes/audit_head_shake_timestep.py --work <folder outside the repo>
motion: tools/head_shake_motion.py (87 frames); the still control has the same length, nothing moves

measures.relative_to_head: run report: per frame, the largest displacement of a free display vertex against the head, minus the settled frame (geometric mm)
measures.curve_difference: shake curve minus still curve, frame by frame
measures.vector_measure: spikes/audit_head_shake.py's measure: per free vertex (shake - carried by the head) - still, largest over the free vertices
measures.settle_step_13_to_14_mm: largest tissue node displacement between frames 13 and 14, physics/positions.npy (geometric mm): the settle is finished when it is near zero
measures.retries: FEBio 'Retrying time step' lines in the run log

motion_between_frames.head_translation: along x, the same for the head and jaw01 drivers
motion_between_frames.interpolation_in_generate_py: linear: every load curve of a rigid-body displacement has one point per frame (<interpolate>LINEAR</interpolate>), so with n substeps the body moves in n equal increments per frame at constant speed
motion_between_frames.consequence: the velocity jumps at every frame sample (zero in the still run); refining the time step does not remove these jumps, it resolves them
motion_between_frames.note: the output is written at frame ends only, so the response inside a frame is not seen

A.description: rhoi 0 (the default, not written into the scene), no physical damping

B.description: rhoi -2 (Newmark, no numerical damping), no physical damping

C.description: the T-28 demonstration: C = 45 /s, rhoi 0.5 (both ours, not the lab's)
